title: Put a parcel's tracking events in the right order

blocks.text: A parcel's tracking page merges three feeds. The line-haul carrier posts JSON such as `{"event": "picked up", "sentAt": 1795300000}`, the courier sends ISO-8601 text with a `Z` or an offset, and the sorting depot's scanners report what their wall clock showed when the parcel went past, such as `2026-11-19T08:20:00`. Customers of the Chicago depot see their parcel arrive at the depot hours before the truck that brought it left, and support keeps finding line-haul events dated 1970.
`ParcelTimeline` already merges and sorts the feeds, and reads the courier's text. Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/ParcelTimeline.java`:

items: `fromSentAt(long)`: the moment a line-haul `sentAt` value names. The carrier's API documentation says it counts whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00Z.
`fromScanner(String)`: the moment at which a scanner of this depot showed the given reading. The depot's zone is passed to the constructor.

blocks.text: When you're done, every event sits at the moment it happened, wherever its feed came from. About two lines in total.

cases.says: courier events and scans from a depot whose clocks run on UTC end up at their moments, in time order
a line-haul sentAt value is read as whole seconds since the epoch
a scanner's clock reading is turned into a moment in the depot's own zone, not read as UTC

origin.section: Instant.parse Accepts Only Text That Names Its Offset

concepts: An epoch number carries no unit: reading seconds with ofEpochMilli (or millis as seconds) gives a valid but wrong instant, and nothing throws.
Wall-clock text without an offset becomes an instant only through the sender's zone; appending Z reads it as UTC and shifts it by the zone's offset.
